Add addr_lng/addr_lat to the final SELECT and to the array_map return shape, and extend the @return list<array{...}> PHPDoc on handle() (:120-121). These are the BOOK coordinates and must stay lexically distinct from the existing out_lng/out_lat, which are the earliest GPS FIX (argMin on timestamp_utc) and are unchanged. Pure output-shape extension: no CTE, join, ranking, or filter change. Docblock: REPLACE the 'Accepted residual gap (DEV-2414, documented not fixed)' paragraph (:44-63) — this ticket closes it — and keep the surrounding reasoning; do not append a second paragraph. Add the accepted boundary from Q2: attribution is frozen at first sighting, so after a mechanism-3 flip both surviving rows can carry the same address_id and DEV-1756's derived COUNT(*) WHERE address_id = ? can read two check-ins for one address at one place in one hour. Keep it sparse (repo owner preference). Add the matcher-layer pin in ScoutCheckInMatchQueryParityTest asserting handle() returns addr_lng/addr_lat equal to the seeded BOOK coordinate while lat/lng equal the FIX coordinate, seeded ~35 m apart so a 'reuse lat/lng' mistake cannot pass. That file uses public function test_*() with #[Group('clickhouse')] #[Group('clarity-scout')] and NO #[Test], and it must seed via its own clarityTable() helper (:446) not the hardcoded clarity literal, or the fixture lands in a database the query never reads. subtasks.title: New migration: add addr_lng/addr_lat and move the unique key onto the election grain
subtasks.approach: NEW migration on the 'platform' connection; NEVER edit the shipped 2026_08_10_170314_create_scout_check_ins_table.php. Add two nullable double columns, DROP unique(kit_id, address_id, hour_bucket), ADD unique(kit_id, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, is_staged) under an EXPLICIT index name. Dropping the old index is MANDATORY, not housekeeping: is_staged is absent from it, so a bucket-migrated address's corrected Direct-side row collides on (kit, address_id, hour) and insertOrIgnore silently drops it — that is the ticket's 'keeps is_staged = true forever'. Explicit name is forced by Postgres's 63-char identifier limit: Laravel's implicit name scout_check_ins_kit_id_addr_lng_addr_lat_hour_bucket_is_staged_unique is 69 chars and would be silently truncated by the server. NO BACKFILL and the columns stay nullable — this is mechanically forced, not a shortcut: Postgres NULLS DISTINCT exempts every legacy row from the new index, whereas a backfill would fail the index build outright because the duplicate rows this bug already wrote are exactly what the new constraint rejects (scout-check-ins-size-bound.md). Keep index(['org_id','address_id']) untouched — DEV-1756's derived per-address COUNT(*) depends on it. Sizing: the table is order 10^3 rows (recorder ran ~2.4 days + ~1.7 hours, schedule currently disabled at routes/console.php:59-66), so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE index-build lock is a non-issue and CONCURRENTLY is unnecessary; the write path is quiescent during the window. Match repo migration convention: anonymous class, no declare(strict_types=1) (see the sibling 2026_08_17_152300 and 2026_08_10_170314 files). BLAST RADIUS: needs Dalton's explicit DDL approval line before any edit; prod has no automated migration path — this is hand-applied, and it must be applied BEFORE the code deploy.

subtasks.title: AC2: cover all three flip mechanisms with two-run, mutated-book tests
subtasks.approach: No existing test invokes the command twice against a MUTATED book, so none of the three mechanisms has any coverage today. Add three #[Test] methods to ScoutRecordCheckInsCommandTest (that file's convention: #[Test] with it_/a_/running_ names, RequiresClickhouse, travelTo, the clarityTable()-based insertHotlist/insertOpenAssignmentAddress/insertScPosition helpers at :75-140), each running scout:record-check-ins twice inside ONE UTC hour with a book mutation between runs. MECHANISM 1 (lower id opens at the same geo/side): seed Direct address 9001 at geo G + one in-radius fix, run, then insertOpenAssignmentAddress(..., addressId: 9000) co-located on the same Direct side, run again — assert count === 1, surviving address_id still 9001, matched_at/created_at identical to run 1. MECHANISM 2 (the frequent one — the winner's order closes): seed co-located Direct 9000 (winner) + 9001 at G, run, DELETE 9000's book row (the rebuild dropping a closed order), run again — assert count === 1, address_id STILL 9000 even though it has left the book, matched_at unchanged. MECHANISM 3 (temporal, per flip-risk-measurement.md: 0 of 4,519,947 book address_ids carry both is_staged values, so it is a label change ACROSS rebuilds, never simultaneous dual-listing): seed co-located Staging 8000 (winner) + 8001 at G on an approved staging partner's hotlist + one in-radius fix, run (persists 8000, is_staged=true), then DELETE 8000's Staging book row and INSERT 8000 onto a NEW Direct hotlist at the SAME geo, run again. Per Q1 the expected end state is TWO rows, one per side, and the assertion must be the full four-part combination: total === 2 (not 1 = today's bug where the Direct row is silently dropped, not 3 = a spurious extra Staging row for 8001) AND exactly one row with is_staged = false AND exactly one with is_staged = true AND the is_staged = true row's matched_at/created_at still equal run 1's. A count-only check, or one that only inspects the new row's label, would each pass a broken design that emitted two STAGING rows and no Direct row — which is the actual failure mode. Book mutations go through DB::connection('clarity_clickhouse') on clarityTable('scout_open_addresses') (ALTER TABLE ... DELETE or a truncate-and-reseed, matching whichever the file already uses for CH mutation); anchor all fixes near now().

subtasks.title: Pin the new key at the Postgres layer: precision guard, geo provenance, AC4, constraint directness
subtasks.approach: Four more #[Test] methods in the same file, serialized after t4 because they share it. (1) POSTGRES PRECISION GUARD — the one failure mode that would silently defeat the whole index: PDO binds floats as strings under precision=14, so the value that lands in Postgres is the 14-significant-digit form, not the exact double (geo-key-float-precision.md). That truncation is deterministic, so under-collapse is impossible, but over-collapse must be pinned: two book addresses ~1 m apart (1e-5 degrees) on the same side/hour must persist as TWO distinct rows, and one place re-run must persist ONE. Assert that BEHAVIOUR, not bit-equality of the stored float — bit-exactness is not what the fix depends on. (2) GEO PROVENANCE at the storage layer: book address at (-97.700000, 30.300000), fix ~35 m away at (-97.7003, 30.3003) (inside the 160.934 m radius) — assert persisted addr_lng/addr_lat === the BOOK pair and lat/lng === the FIX pair. Catches a 'reuse lat/lng as the key' mistake, which would not be idempotent at all since each re-match picks a fresh earliest fix from the sliding window. (3) AC4 REGRESSION: N co-located Direct AND N co-located Staging addresses at one identical geo -> exactly 2 rows, one per side, unchanged by moving the key onto the geo pair. (4) CONSTRAINT DIRECTNESS: a raw duplicate insert on (kit_id, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, is_staged) is rejected by the database itself (expect a QueryException / unique violation), not merely deferred to insertOrIgnore's application-level intent — AC1's guarantee is only as strong as the index, and the recorder runs with 2 concurrent slots so a code-side check would not be race-safe. Same file conventions as t4.
